subject: Merchant connector roadmap alignment & exception path
messages:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Steger <alex.steger@merchsys.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 29 Nov 2026 09:24:00 -0800
Subject: Merchant connector roadmap alignment & exception path

Alex —

Thanks again for the demo last week. We had a follow-up internally and want to align on two things so engineering can prioritize the connector work:

1) Scope: MerchSys requires a non-standard auth handshake (two-step token + signed merchant_id header). We attached our current merchant_api_spec_v2.pdf with the exact fields. Can you confirm whether this is something your connector team can support natively or if it will need an "exception" implementation on our side?

2) Roadmap & timeline: the customer (AcmeRetail) has a go-live window in late Q1. We need an ETA and whether you can support a Canary/limited-scope rollout (one region, low qps) while we finish entitlements.

Action items I need from you by EOD Wed:
- Confirm implementation approach (native vs exception)
- If exception, provide the minimal contract/operational guardrails you require
- Any redlines your security team will flag (we can route to Karthik)

Attached: merchant_api_spec_v2.pdf (summary page + auth flow).

Thanks —
Naomi Feldman
Partner Programs Manager | Redwood Inference
naomi.feldman@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0123
From: Alex Steger <alex.steger@merchsys.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 11:08:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Merchant connector roadmap alignment & exception path

Hi Naomi —

Appreciate the spec. Quick notes after my initial pass:

- Our standard connector stack expects OAuth2 bearer tokens; the two-step token + signed header is not supported out of the box. We can do a small exception layer (middleware in our connector) but it will be a scoped, documented deviation.
- Estimated effort: 2 sprints to prototype + 1 sprint for hardened QA (+ security review). If we start prototyping mid-December we can aim for a Feb canary.
- Security asks: we will need the exact TTL requirements for merchant tokens and a threat model for the signed merchant_id header (please provide if possible).

We can prepare a short "exception snippet" (text) we sign to acknowledge operational responsibilities on both sides — I can share a draft once your legal confirms they're comfortable with a scoped exception.

No attachments from us yet — will send exception draft and timeline doc this week.

Best,
Alex
Head of Integrations | MerchSys
alex.steger@merchsys.com
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 02 Dec 2026 09:36:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: Merchant connector roadmap alignment & exception path

Looping internal product/eng asks into thread — forwarding Alex's note.

Karthik — a couple items for product infra devs so we can scope this correctly:
- Concrete request from partner: support for signed merchant_id header + short-lived token exchange. We should confirm whether this is implementable as a configuration on our gateway (preferred) or requires a custom adapter per-partner.
- If custom adapter: estimate cost and who owns maintenance. Ben suggests dedicated small adapter owned by Integrations team with clear kill-switch and monitoring.
- Security: we need a checklist for the partner exception (audit log retention, token revocation plan, tracing hooks).

Proposed canary plan (for AcmeRetail):
- Stage: us-west only, 05:00–23:00 PST, throttled to 10 rps max
- Observability: token acceptance ratio, error rate, latency percentiles to be reported daily into the Redwood Console
- Rollback: immediate routing to generic fallback connector if errors >2% sustained over 15m

Naomi — can you confirm Acme is okay with the limited regional window? If so, I'll draft the rollout runbook and send to legal for the exception snippet.

—Ben
Ben Carter
Director, Partner Engineering | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai

Naomi / Ben —

Thanks for the proposed canary plan — that works for us. Attached is a signed_exemption_snippet.txt that covers the operational guardrails we require (retention window, incident notification SLA, and a single-point escalation contact). We're happy to sign a short addendum.

Next steps:
- Ben: can you draft the rollout runbook and share with our security team (cc'd) for a quick review?
- Naomi: I'll schedule a 30m sync next week to align timelines and ask items for legal. Here's a placeholder meeting link: https://meet.redwood.ai/naomi-merchsys-sync (calendar invite to follow).
